findings.evidence: template/scripts/sandboxed_writer.py build_profile builds deny_read only from DENY_READ_HOME, protected paths and platform_root. launch_sandboxed_writer reads the token path in read_claude_token but never passes it to build_profile. `~/.config/dev-platform` is denied only by coincidence of the default location. The writer also gets the token in its env, so reading the file is not needed, but the spec requirement is unmet. No test covers it (tests/test_sandboxed_writer.py ProfileTests).
findings.summary: The spec requires "The token file location SHALL be read-denied inside the sandbox", but the generated profile never adds the configured token_file path to denyRead. A token_file outside the hardcoded home entries is readable by the writer.

findings.evidence: proposal.md: "denyWrite ... the push remote path when local". `launch_sandboxed_writer` calls `build_profile(checkout=..., protected=protected_paths(integration_root), platform_root=...)` with no `extra_deny_write`. A bare local origin outside the integration tree and worktrees stays writable only if it lies under an allowWrite root, so the exposure is limited. The proposal and implementation still diverge.
findings.summary: The proposal says the profile write-denies the push remote path when it is local. The launch path never computes it, and `extra_deny_write` is never populated by `launch_sandboxed_writer`.

findings.evidence: sandboxed_writer.py protected_paths runs `git worktree list --porcelain` once. Its result is written to the static srt-settings.json.
findings.summary: Registered worktrees are enumerated once at launch. A worktree created elsewhere during a long writer run is not covered. The `~/.config` and `~/.claude` denies and the realpath checks do not close this for worktrees at arbitrary paths.
